messages:
liz: Heads-up: found an annoying repro in the Python async sample with Dedicated + corporate proxy + custom CA. AsyncClient ignores REDWOOD_BASE_URL and ends up hitting public api.redwood.ai; also SSL verification fails.

liz: env used:
  REDWOOD_BASE_URL=https://dedicated-west.internal
  REDWOOD_CUSTOM_CA=/opt/certs/company-ca.pem
  HTTPS_PROXY=http://proxy.corp:3128

liz: minimal repro:
```py
from redwood import AsyncClient
c = AsyncClient()
await c.chat.create('hi')
```

liz: exception: SSL cert verify failed, then httpx.ConnectError -> api.redwood.ai in traceback. sync Client works fine with same envs.

omar: sounds like httpx transport isn't getting our SSLContext and base_url isn't canonicalized before proxy logic kicks in. we've seen similar in other threads.

petra: quick workaround: pass base_url + ssl_context explicitly when constructing AsyncClient. e.g.
```py
import ssl
from redwood import AsyncClient
sslctx = ssl.create_default_context(cafile='/opt/certs/company-ca.pem')
client = AsyncClient(base_url='https://dedicated-west.internal', _transport_kwargs={'ssl_context': sslctx, 'proxies': {'https':'http://proxy.corp:3128'}})
```

petra: but agree it's not ideal to surface _transport_kwargs. we should expose typed transport_kwargs or handle CA/proxy wiring inside the SDK.

omar: I'll open a PR: ensure AsyncClient(...) always sets base_url from explicit arg or env before any proxy handling, build ssl.SSLContext from REDWOOD_CUSTOM_CA and pass into AsyncHTTPTransport when proxies are present, and add mypy stubs so the ctor typing matches.

liz: thanks — will test the patch. please add an alpine CI matrix test too; musl CA differences bit us before.

typebot: created PR #4444: async/httpx: propagate REDWOOD_CUSTOM_CA into AsyncHTTPTransport when proxied; canonicalize base_url early; add alpine integ test (draft).

ci-bot: ci/sample-app: linux-integ ✅, alpine-integ ❌ (ssl verify failed).

liz: noted — will re-run once tests land.
